studyType: Patient information page (NHS website), not a study or guideline
supports: Get advice from NHS 111 now if the knee is badly swollen or has changed shape.
Get advice from NHS 111 now if the knee locks, gives way or painfully clicks; painless clicking is normal.
Get advice from NHS 111 now if the knee is very painful, or you cannot move it or put any weight on it.
Get advice from NHS 111 now if there is a very high temperature with redness or heat around the knee (possible infection).
See a GP if knee pain does not improve within a few weeks.
doesNotSupport: Pain at rest or at night as a reason to seek care.
Numbness or tingling down the leg as a reason to seek care.
Any time frame more precise than 'a few weeks' (for example '2–3 weeks').
Onset after a twist, fall or impact as a reason to seek care on its own.
limits: General knee pain advice for the public, not specific to runners or ITBS.
Routes readers to UK services (NHS 111, GP); the urgency levels carry over, the services do not.
